name: Idiopathic Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension with BMPR2 Mutation
aliases: Heritable Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension with BMPR2 Mutation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: European Society of Cardiology/European Respiratory Society (ESC/ERS) Guidelines for Pulmonary Hypertension

criteria.description: Mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) ≥ 20 mmHg at rest measured by right heart catheterization
Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) ≤ 15 mmHg to exclude left heart disease
Presence of pathogenic BMPR2 gene mutation confirmed by genetic testing
Exclusion of other causes of pulmonary hypertension including connective tissue disease, congenital heart disease, and chronic thromboembolic disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Hemodynamic confirmation by right heart catheterization with mPAP ≥ 20 mmHg, PCWP ≤ 15 mmHg, PVR ≥ 3 Wood units, exclusion of secondary causes, and supportive genetic testing for BMPR2 mutation if available
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is recommended for family screening and prognostic assessment but is not mandatory for diagnosis.

pathognomonic.notes: Progressive shortness of breath on exertion is a hallmark symptom

pathognomonic.symptomName: Fatigue related to reduced cardiac output
searchTerms: fatigue due to low cardiac output

pathognomonic.notes: Indicative of advanced disease and right ventricular failure

occasional.symptomName: Abdominal distension due to hepatomegaly or ascites
searchTerms: belly bloating due to liver or fluid

occasional.notes: May be present in some patients with connective tissue overlap

rare.symptomName: Hoarseness due to recurrent laryngeal nerve compression
searchTerms: voice changes due to nerve pressure

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) or NT-proBNP indicating right ventricular strain
Mild hypoxemia on arterial blood gas analysis
imaging: Right ventricular hypertrophy and dilation on echocardiography
Enlarged pulmonary arteries on chest CT or chest X-ray
Perfusion defects excluded by ventilation-perfusion scan
genetic: Pathogenic BMPR2 gene mutation identified by molecular genetic testing
other: Right heart catheterization confirming elevated pulmonary arterial pressures and vascular resistance

distinguishingFeatures: Ventilation-perfusion scan showing mismatched perfusion defects
Elevated pulmonary capillary wedge pressure > 15 mmHg
Echocardiographic evidence of left heart dysfunction
Common in older patients with heart failure

redFlags: Signs of right heart failure such as severe peripheral edema or ascites
Sudden onset chest pain or hemoptysis
references: Simonneau G, et al. Haemodynamic definitions and updated clinical classification of pulmonary hypertension. Eur Respir J. 2019.
Machado RD, et al. Genetics and genomics of pulmonary arterial hypertension. Eur Respir J. 2015.
European Society of Cardiology/European Respiratory Society Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary hypertension. Eur Heart J. 2022.
